A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Free Hunch, with matching authors, methods and retained experiments. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic posterior-sampling experiments and ImageNet restoration results, including Figures 5 and 8 and Table 1.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic experiments, expanded ImageNet comparisons and direct covariance-error measurements, including Tables 1–3 and Figures 11–12.

M1.justification: The time updates, BFGS space updates, DCT initialization, low-rank representation and guidance fallback remain unchanged. New Algorithms 3–4 document the existing pipeline. The extra-evaluation toy variant was already disclosed in v1 Appendix F.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix G adds a different two-dimensional Gaussian-mixture prior and likelihood configuration, illustrated in Figure 10, alongside the retained Figure 2 example. ImageNet 256×256 and the four image-restoration tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 2–3 add evaluated DDNM+ and DiffPIR comparisons to the retained DPS, ΠGDM, TMPD and two Peng baselines, substantially broadening comparison beyond covariance-based reconstruction guidance. DDNM+ has Gaussian-deblurring, inpainting and super-resolution results, but no motion-deblurring results.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the reported test sample from 100 to 1,000 images. Appendix H expands image evaluation from 15/30-step Heun sampling to Euler and Heun at 15, 30, 50 and 100 steps. Appendix G adds Frobenius covariance-error evaluation and deterministic versus stochastic sampling protocols, including 25–400-step comparisons.

E4.justification: New Appendix G directly tests initialization, space updates and errors from transferring score evaluations across time, then compares deterministic and stochastic sampling using the two-evaluation variant. Appendix H expands DPS guidance sensitivity and adds DiffPIR and Identity/Identity+Online parameter sweeps in Figures 13–16.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained posterior-standard-deviation analysis concerns distribution calibration; the new covariance-error curves measure approximation accuracy rather than uncertainty in reported experimental estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes substantially: for example, 15-step FH Gaussian-deblurring PSNR changes from 22.68 to 23.39 and LPIPS from 0.353 to 0.372. These accompany the larger evaluation sample and do not establish same-setting performance gains. Tables 2–3, covariance-error plots, expanded sensitivity curves and FH+Online qualitative examples add substantial results.

T1.justification: v2 corrects Equation 18 by including the missing multiplication by Δx and restores inverse-Hessian factors in Appendix A's mean-update derivation, comparing v1 Equation 50 with v2 Equation 48. The principal derivations remain; no new convergence theorem or covariance-error bound is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: efficient training-free covariance estimation, analysis of covariance-induced guidance bias, and improved linear inverse-problem recovery, especially at low step counts. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains stochastic sampling's richer directional curvature information, motivates DCT and BFGS against alternatives, and discusses DDNM+'s measurement-operator limitations. The original applicability and error-bound limitations remain. Section 4.2 also strengthens performance wording to 'across all metrics', although Peng still leads FH variants in 30-step motion-deblurring PSNR.

D1.justification: v2 adds end-to-end Euler and solver-independent pseudocode, explicit schedule parameters, a code-availability link, and fuller tuning documentation using 100 validation images and LPIPS-based selection. Existing conjugate-gradient schedules, BFGS update ranges and hardware disclosures are retained. These additions substantially expand implementation documentation.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds work on principal-component covariance estimation, audio editing, causal discovery, higher-order score matching and Fisher information, including Manor and Michaeli's papers. Appendix I adds JPEG and quasi-Newton references. The four-category taxonomy and central research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Several background, method and results paragraphs are tightened, notation explanations are added, and author formatting, publication headers and acknowledgments change. New appendix sections are inserted and existing ones renumbered, while the main section order and argument remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2–3, Algorithms 3–4 and a substantial covariance-error and parameter-sensitivity figure suite. Figures 7 and 9 gain an FH+Online column. The earlier DPS Figure 11 is expanded into Figure 13, while the earlier guidance-metric Figure 10 is retained as Figure 17.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central covariance-estimation proposal: direct error ablations expose component and sampler effects, while the larger image evaluation covers additional comparison methods and sampling budgets. Algebra corrections and fuller implementation documentation improve assessability. These gains outweigh overbroad performance wording and inconsistent variables in the new pseudocode. The stochastic convergence evidence remains limited to the extra-evaluation toy variant, rather than establishing convergence of standard FH.
